speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing knee pain after recently increasing your physical activity. To help me determine the cause, could you tell me exactly where the pain is located and describe the specific type of pain you feel, such as sharp, dull, or aching?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of volleyball with repetitive pivoting, is the pain localized to the medial (inner) side of the knee, and does it worsen when you twist your leg or bear weight? Also, have you noticed any swelling or hearing a "pop" at the onset of pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)

Based on your description of pain located on the medial aspect of the tibia inferior to the patella, combined with your recent increase in physical activity and volleyball participation, this presentation is highly suggestive of Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome. Could you confirm if the pain is diffuse along the bone or strictly at a specific insertion point, and does it improve with rest?
